The student plays Black and just made a move.

Position before their move (FEN): r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/2b1p3/2B1P3/3P1N2/PPP2PPP/RNBQ1RK1 b kq - 2 5

A. Gemini alone.text: Taking the center pawn with ...Nxe4 certainly creates some tactical complexity, but it actually allows White to gain a significant initiative after d4. By attacking your knight and bishop simultaneously, White forces you to give up your strong piece activity or lose material. You would have been in much better shape had you simply played d6 to bolster your center and develop your pieces naturally. Since we are in this position now, how do you plan to respond to d4 to keep your knight from being trapped?
